source.snippet: "I'm troubleshooting a website that occasionally returns 5xx errors during traffic spikes. Googlebot is still crawling the site, but some URLs are taking longer to be discovered and indexed. How should I diagnose whether these intermittent errors are affecting Googlebot's crawl rate or causing indexing delays?"

problem_statement: SEO practitioners and site owners lack clear tooling to correlate intermittent server-side 5xx errors with measurable drops in Googlebot crawl rate and indexing delays, forcing manual log analysis and guesswork when organic traffic suffers.
target_segment: Technical SEO consultants and in-house SEO managers at SMBs and agencies running sites with variable traffic loads.
notes: Buyer signal: two questions from the same author (Ali Raza) on serverfault and webmasters.SE within 24 hours on related crawl/indexing topics suggests an agency or consultant actively billing a client for this diagnostic work. SEO agencies routinely pay for tools (Screaming Frog, Sitebulb, etc.) — a lightweight crawl-health-to-indexing-correlation monitor would fit existing paid-tool buying patterns. Signal is thin (two posts, one author) but topical cluster is well-established.
